[SOL]
'Although' or 'Though' is followed by 'yet' or a comma (,), not by 'but'. Remove 'but'.
उदा. 'Although/Though' के साथ वाक्य में 'but' का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता है, इसके स्थान पर 'yet' या अल्पविराम (,) का प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Superfluous Conjunctions

---

[Q1278] This is the same book / which I wanted / to buy yesterday. / No Error
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) This is the same book
(b) which I wanted
(c) to buy yesterday.
(d) No Error
[ANS] b
[SOL]
After words like 'same', 'all', 'only', 'any', 'none', the relative pronoun used is 'that' instead of 'who' or 'which'. Replace 'which' with 'that'.
उदा. 'the same', 'all', 'only' आदि शब्दों के बाद relative pronoun के रूप में 'which' या 'who' की बजाय 'that' का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
[RULE] Relative Pronouns Usage

---

[Q1279] Hardly had I stepped out / than it started / raining heavily. / No Error
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) Hardly had I stepped out
(b) than it started
(c) raining heavily.
(d) No Error
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'Hardly/Scarcely' must be followed by 'when' or 'before', not 'than'. Replace 'than' with 'when'.
उदा. 'Hardly' के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग होता है, 'than' का नहीं।
[RULE] Adverbial Correlatives

---

[Q1280] Neither the girl / nor her parents was / present at the function / which was held yesterday.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Neither the girl
(b) nor her parents was
(c) present at the function
(d) which was held yesterday.
[ANS] b
[SOL]
When subjects are joined by 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. 'Parents' is plural, so 'were' should be used instead of 'was'.
उदा. 'Neither...nor' में verb पास वाले subject के अनुसार आती है। 'parents' plural है, अतः 'was' की जगह 'were' होगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement

---

[Q1281] The company has / launched a new eco-friendly / car in the market / few months ago.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) The company has
(b) launched a new eco-friendly
(c) car in the market
(d) few months ago.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
An action completed in the past with a specific past time marker ('ago') takes the Simple Past Tense, not Present Perfect. Replace 'has launched' with 'launched'.
उदा. भूतकाल के निश्चित समय (ago) दर्शाने वाले वाक्य में Past Indefinite Tense का प्रयोग होता है, Present Perfect का नहीं।
[RULE] Tenses

---

[Q1282] She is more taller / than her sister / who works in / the same office.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) She is more taller
(b) than her sister
(c) who works in
(d) the same office.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Double comparatives are incorrect. 'Taller' is already comparative, so 'more' is redundant. Remove 'more'.
उदा. एक साथ दो comparative words ('more' और 'taller') का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता। 'more' को हटा दें।
[RULE] Superfluous Expressions / Adjectives

---

[Q1283] One of the most / challenging task for / me is to learn / a foreign language.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) One of the most
(b) challenging task for
(c) me is to learn
(d) a foreign language.
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The phrase 'one of' is always followed by a plural noun. Replace 'task' with 'tasks'.
उदा. 'one of' के बाद हमेशा plural noun का प्रयोग होता है। 'task' की जगह 'tasks' का प्रयोग करें।
[RULE] Nouns

---

[Q1284] Hardly had I stepped / out of the house / when a heavy downpour / starts.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Hardly had I stepped
(b) out of the house
(c) when a heavy downpour
(d) starts.
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The sentence is in the past tense ('had I stepped'). Therefore, the second clause must also be in the past tense. Replace 'starts' with 'started'.
उदा. वाक्य का पहला भाग Past Tense में है, इसलिए दूसरा भाग भी Past Tense में होना चाहिए। 'starts' के स्थान पर 'started' होगा।
[RULE] Sequence of Tenses

---

[Q1285] The teacher told the / students that the earth / revolved around / the sun.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) The teacher told the
(b) students that the earth
(c) revolved around
(d) the sun.
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Universal truths and scientific facts always remain in the Simple Present Tense, even in indirect speech. Replace 'revolved' with 'revolves'.
उदा. सार्वभौमिक सत्य (Universal truth) हमेशा Present Indefinite Tense में रहते हैं। 'revolved' की जगह 'revolves' होगा।
[RULE] Direct & Indirect / Tenses

---

[Q1286] He is capable to do / this work within / the given period / of two weeks.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) He is capable to do
(b) this work within
(c) the given period
(d) of two weeks.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The adjective 'capable' is followed by the preposition 'of' and a gerund (V1+ing), not 'to'. Replace 'capable to do' with 'capable of doing'.
उदा. Adjective 'capable' के बाद preposition 'of' और gerund (-ing form) आता है, न कि 'to'।
[RULE] Fixed Prepositions

---

[Q1287] Unless you do not / read the instructions carefully, / you cannot answer / the questions correctly.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Unless you do not
(b) read the instructions carefully,
(c) you cannot answer
(d) the questions correctly.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Unless' is a negative conditional word and already implies 'if not'. Never use 'not' in the clause containing 'unless'. Remove 'do not'.
उदा. 'Unless' का अर्थ नकारात्मक होता है, इसलिए इसके साथ 'not' का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता। 'do not' हटाएं।
[RULE] Conditionals / Superfluous

---

[Q1288] The team has been working on the project since last year.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A. has been working
(b) B. on the project
(c) C. since last year
(d) D. None of these
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: Subject–verb agreement – a plural noun (team) requires a plural verb form.
उदाहरण: "The teams have been working." यहाँ ‘teams’ बहुवचन है, अतः ‘have been’ सही है।
[RULE] Subject-verb agreement (plural)

---

[Q1289] She don't like going to the movies on rainy days.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A. She don't
(b) B. like going
(c) C. to the movies
(d) D. on rainy days
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: Subject–verb agreement – ‘she’ is singular, verb should be singular: ‘does not’.
उदाहरण: "She does not like" – यहाँ ‘does’ एकवचन है।
[RULE] Subject-verb agreement (singular)

---

[Q1290] Neither the manager nor the employees was aware of the changes.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A. Neither the manager
(b) B. nor the employees
(c) C. was aware
(d) D. of the changes
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Rule: With ‘neither…nor’, the verb agrees with the nearer subject; here ‘employees’ is plural, so use ‘were’. 
उदाहरण: "Neither the manager nor the employees were aware."
[RULE] Verb agreement with neither…nor

---

[Q1291] He has gone to the supermarket, and bought some groceries.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A. has gone
(b) B. to the supermarket
(c) C. and bought
(d) D. some groceries
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Rule: Two independent clauses joined by ‘and’ should each have a subject; the second clause is missing a subject. 
उदाहरण: "He has gone, and he bought some groceries."
[RULE] Compound sentence – missing subject

---

[Q1292] The committee has to decide on the budget, but they are not yet ready.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A. The committee
(b) B. has to decide
(c) C. but they are
(d) D. not yet ready
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule: ‘committee’ is singular, so the verb should be ‘has decided’ or ‘has to decide’. The construction is fine; the error lies in the tense mismatch. 
उदाहरण: "The committee has decided…"
[RULE] Subject–verb agreement (singular)

---

[Q1293] The students, along with the teachers, has gathered in the hall.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A. The students, along with the teachers
(b) B. has gathered
(c) C. in the hall
(d) D. None of these
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule: When a plural noun is followed by a phrase in parentheses, the verb agrees with the first noun; here ‘students’ is plural, so use ‘have gathered’. 
उदाहरण: "The students, along with the teachers, have gathered…"
[RULE] Plural verb agreement after parenthetical phrase

---

[Q1294] I am looking forward to the week end but we will have to postpone our meeting.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A. I am looking forward
(b) B. to the weekend
(c) C. but we will have
(d) D. postpone our meeting
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Rule: Two independent clauses joined by ‘but’ should each have a subject; the second clause correctly has a subject. The error is actually that the first clause is incomplete – it lacks a subject? No, the error is that the second clause uses ‘will have’ but should be ‘will have to’. 
उदाहरण: "…but we will have to postpone…"
[RULE] Modal verb usage (have to)

---

[Q1295] She will goes to the conference next month.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A. She will
(b) B. goes
(c) C. to the conference
(d) D. next month
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule: After ‘will’, the base form of the verb is used; ‘goes’ is incorrect. 
उदाहरण: "She will go to the conference."
[RULE] Future tense – base form after will

---

[Q1296] The jury has been deciding the case for weeks, and they has reached a verdict.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A. The jury has been deciding
(b) B. for weeks
(c) C. and they has reached
(d) D. a verdict
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Rule: ‘jury’ is singular, but the verb should be ‘has reached’ (singular). The error is the verb ‘has’ with plural subject ‘they’. 
उदाहरण: "and they have reached a verdict."
[RULE] Subject–verb agreement (plural vs singular)

---

[Q1297] The manager, as well as the staff, are going to the work shop
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2021 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A. The manager, as well as the staff
(b) B. are going
(c) C. to the workshop
(d) D. None of these
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule: When a singular noun is followed by a phrase with ‘as well as’, the verb agrees with the singular noun; thus use ‘is going’. 
उदाहरण: "The manager, as well as the staff, is going…"
[RULE] Verb agreement with as well as

---

[Q1298] Hardly had I arrived / at the station than / the train departed. / No error
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) Hardly had I arrived
(b) at the station than
(c) the train departed
(d) No error
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The correlative conjunction for 'Hardly/Scarcely' is 'when', not 'than'. 'Than' is used with 'No sooner'. Therefore, replace 'than' with 'when' in part (B).
उदा. 'Hardly' या 'Scarcely' के साथ 'when' का प्रयोग होता है, न कि 'than' का। 'than' का प्रयोग 'No sooner' के साथ किया जाता है। अतः (B) में 'than' के स्थान पर 'when' होगा।
[RULE] Hardly/Scarcely ... when

---

[Q1299] One of the most important / task in the project / has been completed successfully. / No error
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) One of the most important
(b) task in the project
(c) has been completed successfully
(d) No error
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The phrase 'One of' is always followed by a plural noun. Here, 'task' should be plural 'tasks'.
उदा. 'One of' के बाद हमेशा Plural Noun (बहुवचन संज्ञा) का प्रयोग किया जाता है। इसलिए 'task' की जगह 'tasks' होना चाहिए।
[RULE] One of + Plural Noun

---

[Q1300] Neither the teacher / nor the students was / present in the class. / No error
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Neither the teacher
(b) nor the students was
(c) present in the class
(d) No error
[ANS] b
[SOL]
When two subjects are joined by 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearest subject. Here, the nearest subject is 'students' (plural), so the verb should be 'were' instead of 'was'.
उदा. जब दो सब्जेक्ट्स 'neither...nor' से जुड़े हों, तो वर्ब पास वाले सब्जेक्ट के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ पास वाला सब्जेक्ट 'students' (plural) है, इसलिए 'was' की जगह 'were' आएगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement with Neither...Nor

---

[Q1301] She is more taller / than her sister / in every aspect. / No error
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) She is more taller
(b) than her sister
(c) in every aspect
(d) No error
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Double comparatives are incorrect. 'Tall' is a single-syllable adjective, so its comparative form is 'taller'. Using 'more' before 'taller' is superfluous.
उदा. एक साथ दो Comparative Degrees ('more' और 'taller') का प्रयोग एक साथ नहीं किया जा सकता। 'taller' अपने आप में सही है, इसलिए 'more' हटाना होगा।
[RULE] Superfluous Comparative

---

[Q1302] Each of the boys / have submitted / their assignments on time. / No error
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Each of the boys
(b) have submitted
(c) their assignments on time
(d) No error
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'Each of' takes a singular verb and singular pronoun. Replace 'have' with 'has'.
उदा. 'Each of' के बाद Plural Noun आता है लेकिन Verb और Pronoun हमेशा Singular (एकवचन) होते हैं। अतः 'have' की जगह 'has' का प्रयोग होगा।
[RULE] Each of + Singular Verb

---

[Q1303] He told to me / that he would help me / with my home work. / No error
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) He told to me
(b) that he would help me
(c) with my homework
(d) No error
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The verb 'tell' does not take a preposition 'to' when followed by an object. It should be 'He told me', not 'He told to me'.
उदा. 'Tell' वर्ब के बाद सीधे ऑब्जेक्ट आता है, इसके साथ 'to' प्रीपोजिशन का प्रयोग नहीं होता है। अतः 'told to me' गलत है, 'told me' सही है।
[RULE] Transitive Verb 'Tell'

---

[Q1304] No sooner did the sun rise / when the fog disappeared / completely from the valley. / No error
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) No sooner did the sun rise
(b) when the fog disappeared
(c) completely from the valley
(d) No error
[ANS] b
[SOL]
'No sooner' must be followed by 'than', not 'when'. Replace 'when' with 'than' in part (B).
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ हमेशा 'than' का प्रयोग होता है, न कि 'when' का। अतः (B) में 'when' के स्थान पर 'than' होगा।
[RULE] No sooner ... than

---

[Q1305] Despite of working hard / he failed to secure / the first rank in the exam. / No error
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) Despite of working hard
(b) he failed to secure
(c) the first rank in the exam
(d) No error
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. (In spite of = Despite). Therefore, 'Despite of' is incorrect and should be changed to 'Despite' or 'In spite of'.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता है ('In spite of' होता है)। अतः 'Despite of' के स्थान पर केवल 'Despite' का प्रयोग होगा।
[RULE] Despite vs In spite of

---

[Q1306] It is high time / you start preparing / for your upcoming examinations. / No error
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) It is high time
(b) you start preparing
(c) for your upcoming examinations
(d) No error
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Expressions like 'It is time', 'It is high time', 'It is about time' are followed by a clause in the Simple Past tense (V2). Replace 'start' with 'started'.
उदा. 'It is high time' या 'It is time' के बाद आने वाला उपवाक्य (clause) हमेशा Past Indefinite Tense (V2) में होता है। अतः 'start' की जगह 'started' होगा।
[RULE] It is high time + Past Tense

---

[Q1307] The committee is / divided in their opinions / regarding the new policy. / No error
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) The committee is
(b) divided in their opinions
(c) regarding the new policy
(d) No error
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When a collective noun like 'committee' is divided in opinion or acts as individuals, it takes a plural verb and plural pronoun ('their'). Therefore, 'is' should be changed to 'are'.
उदा. जब Collective Noun (जैसे committee) में मतभेद हो जाए या अलग-अलग सदस्यों की बात हो, तो उसके साथ Plural Verb का प्रयोग होता है। अतः 'is' की जगह 'are' होगा।
[RULE] Collective Noun with Division

---

[Q1308] Hardly had I / stepped out of the house / when a heavy downpour / ruined my clothes.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) (A)
(b) (B)
(c) (C)
(d) (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
No error in this part. The correlative conjunction 'Hardly' is correctly followed by 'had + subject + V3' and 'when'. 
उदा. 'Hardly/Scarcely' के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग होता है और वाक्य की शुरुआत में आने पर inversion नियम (had + subject) लागू होता है। यहाँ कोई गलती नहीं है, इसलिए वाक्य 'No Error' श्रेणी में है या फिर ऑप्शन (D) सही है यदि कोई अन्य त्रुटि हो। (Assuming error-free standard format).
[RULE] Conjunction (Hardly... when)

---

[Q1309] She told to me / a very interesting / story about her / childhood days.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) (A)
(b) (B)
(c) (C)
(d) (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Replace 'told to me' with 'told me'. The verb 'tell' does not take a preposition 'to' before its indirect object, unlike 'say to me'.
उदा. 'Tell' के बाद सीधा object आता है, बीच में 'to' का प्रयोग नहीं होता है ('told me' सही है, 'told to me' गलत)।
[RULE] Verbs followed by Prepositions

---

[Q1310] One of the most / popular leaders who / is alive today / is Mahatma Gandhi.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) (A)
(b) (B)
(c) (C)
(d) (D)
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Replace 'is' with 'are'. The verb in a relative clause ('who') agrees with its antecedent ('leaders', which is plural). Therefore, 'are' should be used.
उदा. Relative pronoun ('who') से पहले आए Antecedent ('leaders') के अनुसार verb plural ('are') होगी, न कि singular ('is')।
[RULE] Relative Pronoun & Subject-Verb Agreement

---

[Q1311] Each of the students / in the science class / have submitted their / assignment on time.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) (A)
(b) (B)
(c) (C)
(d) (D)
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Replace 'have submitted their' with 'has submitted his/her'. 'Each' is singular, so it takes a singular verb ('has') and singular possessive pronoun ('his/her').
उदा. 'Each of' के बाद noun plural होता है लेकिन verb और pronoun हमेशा singular होते हैं। इसलिए 'have' की जगह 'has' और 'their' की जगह 'his/her' होगा।
[RULE] Pronoun & Verb Agreement with 'Each'

---

[Q1312] Despite of working hard / he failed to secure / the first rank in / the final examination.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) (A)
(b) (B)
(c) (C)
(d) (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Replace 'Despite of' with 'Despite' or 'In spite of'. 'Despite' is never followed by 'of', whereas 'In spite' is always followed by 'of'.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ कभी भी 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं होता है। सही रूप या तो 'Despite working hard' होगा या 'In spite of working hard' होगा।
[RULE] Prepositions (Despite vs In spite of)

---

[Q1313] The number of accidents / on the national highway / have increased significantly / over the past year.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) (A)
(b) (B)
(c) (C)
(d) (D)
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Replace 'have' with 'has'. 'The number of' takes a singular verb, whereas 'A number of' takes a plural verb.
उदा. 'The number of' के साथ singular verb ('has') का प्रयोग होता है, जबकि 'A number of' के साथ plural verb आती है।
[RULE] Determiners & Subject-Verb Agreement

---

[Q1314] Scarcely had I reached / the ticket counter when / the clerk closed / the booking window.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XI (2023)]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) (A)
(b) (B)
(c) (C)
(d) (D)
[ANS] d
[SOL]
No error in this segment. The structure 'Scarcely had + subject + V3 ... when ...' is completely correct.
उदा. 'Scarcely' के साथ 'when' का सही प्रयोग हुआ है और past perfect tense का नियम भी सटीक है। वाक्य त्रुटi-रहित है।
[RULE] Adverbs and Conjunctions

---

[Q1315] She is / more smarter / than her / younger sister.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) She is
(b) more smarter
(c) than her
(d) younger sister.
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Do not use double comparatives. 'Smart' already takes '-er' to form its comparative degree ('smarter'), so 'more' is redundant.
उदा. दो कम्पेरेटिव डिग्री का प्रयोग एक साथ नहीं किया जाता है। 'smart' की कम्पेरेटिव 'smarter' है, इसलिए 'more' का प्रयोग गलत है।
[RULE] Superfluous Comparatives

---

[Q1316] One of my friends / are going / to the USA / next month.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) One of my friends
(b) are going
(c) to the USA
(d) next month.
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The phrase 'One of' is followed by a plural noun and a singular verb. Replace 'are' with 'is'.
उदा. 'One of' के बाद नाउन प्लुरल होता है लेकिन वर्ब हमेशा सिंगुलर होती है। 'are' की जगह 'is' का प्रयोग होगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (One of + Plural Noun + Singular Verb)

---

[Q1317] Hardly had I / reached the station / than the train / started moving.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Hardly had I
(b) reached the station
(c) than the train
(d) started moving.
[ANS] c
[SOL]
The correlative conjunction for 'Hardly' or 'Scarcely' is 'when' or 'before', not 'than'. Replace 'than' with 'when'.
उदा. 'Hardly' या 'Scarcely' के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग होता है, 'than' का नहीं (than का प्रयोग 'No sooner' के साथ होता है)।
[RULE] Correlative Conjunctions (Hardly... when)

---

[Q1318] The manager as well as / his subordinates / were present / at the meeting.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) The manager as well as
(b) his subordinates
(c) were present
(d) at the meeting.
[ANS] c
[SOL]
When subjects are joined by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject ('The manager'). Replace 'were' with 'was'.
उदा. जब दो सब्जेक्ट्स 'as well as' से जुड़ते हैं, तो वर्ब पहले सब्जेक्ट के अनुसार आती है। यहाँ 'The manager' सिंगुलर है, इसलिए 'were' की जगह 'was' आएगा।
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (as well as)

---

[Q1319] No sooner did / the sun rise / when we resumed / our journey.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Easy]
(a) No sooner did
(b) the sun rise
(c) when we resumed
(d) our journey.
[ANS] c
[SOL]
The correlative conjunction for 'No sooner' is 'than', not 'when'. Replace 'when' with 'than'.
उदा. 'No sooner' के साथ हमेशा 'than' का प्रयोग किया जाता है, 'when' का नहीं।
[RULE] Conjunctions (No sooner... than)

---

[Q1320] He asked me / where was I going / during the / summer vacation.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) He asked me
(b) where was I going
(c) during the
(d) summer vacation.
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In indirect speech, the structure of the reported clause should be assertive (Subject + Verb), not interrogative. Change 'where was I going' to 'where I was going'.
उदा. इनडायरेक्ट स्पीच में प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य साधारण वाक्य बन जाता है (Subject + Verb)। 'where was I going' की जगह 'where I was going' होगा।
[RULE] Indirect Speech Sentence Structure

---

[Q1321] Despite of working / very hard, he / failed to clear / the competitive exam.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Despite of working
(b) very hard, he
(c) failed to clear
(d) the competitive exam.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. (In place of 'Despite of', use 'In spite of' or simply 'Despite'). Remove 'of'.
उदा. 'Despite' के साथ 'of' का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता है। 'In spite of' का अर्थ और 'Despite' का अर्थ समान होता है, लेकिन despite के बाद 'of' नहीं आता।
[RULE] Preposition Usage (Despite vs In spite of)

[Q1322] If I was you, / I would not / tolerate such / nonsense behavior.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2023]
[DIFFICULTY: Hard]
(a) If I was you,
(b) I would not
(c) tolerate such
(d) nonsense behavior.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In conditional sentences expressing an imaginary situation, 'were' is used with all subjects. Replace 'was' with 'were'.
उदा. काल्पनिक शर्त (Hypothetical sentence) वाले वाक्यों में सभी सब्जेक्ट्स के साथ 'were' का प्रयोग होता है, चाहे सब्जेक्ट सिंगुलर ही क्यों न हो।
[RULE] Subjunctive Mood / Conditional Sentences

[Q1323] The committee of managers was given a week to submit the report.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) The committee of managers were given a week to submit the report.
(b) The committee of managers was given a week to submit the report.
(c) The committee of managers was given a week to submit the reports.
(d) The committee of managers were given a week to submit the reports.
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The subject ‘committee’ is a collective noun and is treated as singular. Hence the verb should be ‘was’. 
उदा. समिति को रिपोर्ट जमा करने के लिए एक सप्ताह दिया गया।
[RULE] Subject–verb agreement with collective noun

[Q1324] Neither the students nor the teacher were prepared for the examination.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Neither the students nor the teacher were prepared for the examination.
(b) Neither the students nor the teacher was prepared for the examination.
(c) Neither the students nor the teacher have prepared for the examination.
(d) Neither the students nor the teacher has prepared for the examination.
[ANS] b
[SOL]
When two subjects are joined by ‘neither…nor’, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. ‘Teacher’ is singular, so use ‘was’. 
उदा. न तो छात्रों ने परीक्षा की तैयारी की, न ही शिक्षक ने।
[RULE] Verb agreement with neither…nor

[Q1325] The data is collected every month to analyze the trend.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) The data is collected every month to analyze the trend.
(b) The data are collected every month to analyze the trend.
(c) The data is collected every month to analyze the trends.
(d) Zealous
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The word ‘data’ is singular in this context (a mass noun), so use ‘is’. 
उदा. डेटा हर महीने एकत्र किया जाता है।
[RULE] Singular vs plural form of data

[Q1326] The children has been playing in the park all after no on.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) The children has been playing in the park all afternoon.
(b) The children have been playing in the park all afternoon.
(c) The child has been playing in the park all afternoon.
(d) The children has been played in the park all afternoon.
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The subject ‘children’ is plural, so the verb should be ‘have’. 
उदा. बच्चे पूरे दोपहर पार्क में खेल रहे हैं।
[RULE] Subject–verb agreement with plural noun

[Q1327] He suggested that we should stay at home not to catch the flu.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) He suggested that we should stay at home not to catch the flu.
(b) He suggested that we should stay at home to not catch the flu.
(c) He suggested that we should stay at home not catching the flu.
(d) He suggested that we should stay at home to not catching the flu.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When ‘suggest’ is followed by a clause, the infinitive should not have ‘to’. 
उदा. उसने सुझाव दिया कि हमें फ्लू से बचने के लिए घर पर रहना चाहिए।
[RULE] Infinitive after suggest

[Q1328] The manager, along with his staff, have decided to resign.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) The manager, along with his staff, have decided to resign.
(b) The manager, along with his staff, has decided to resign.
(c) Munificent
(d) Nefarious
[ANS] b
[SOL]
When a singular subject is joined by a prepositional phrase, the verb remains singular. Use ‘has’. 
उदा. मैनेजर, साथ में अपने स्टाफ के, इस्तीफा देने का निर्णय लिया।
[RULE] Verb agreement with singular subject + prepositional phrase

[Q1329] The results of the experiment were inconclusive, so we will have to conduct the test again.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) The results of the experiment were inconclusive, so we will have to conduct the test again.
(b) The results of the experiment was inconclusive, so we will have to conduct the test again.
(c) Timid
(d) Uncanny
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The plural noun ‘results’ requires the verb ‘were’. 
उदा. प्रयोग के परिणाम अनिश्चित थे, इसलिए हमें परीक्षण फिर से करना होगा।
[RULE] Subject–verb agreement with plural nouns

[Q1330] She said that he will come tomorrow if he could finish his work.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) She said that he will come tomorrow if he could finish his work.
(b) She said that he would come tomorrow if he could finish his work.
(c) Diligent
(d) Resilient
[ANS] b
[SOL]
In reported speech, the future ‘will’ changes to ‘would’ after a past reporting verb. 
उदा. उसने कहा कि वह अपना काम पूरा कर सके तो वह कल आएगा।
[RULE] Reported speech: will → would

[Q1331] The library provides books, magazines, and newspapers to the students.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) The library provides books, magazines, and newspapers to the students.
(b) The library provide books, magazines, and newspapers to the students.
(c) The library provides books, magazines, and newspapers to the student.
(d) The library provides books, magazines, and newspaper to the students.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The subject ‘library’ is singular, so use ‘provides’. 
उदा. पुस्तकालय छात्रों को पुस्तकें, पत्रिकाएँ और अखबार उपलब्ध कराता है।
[RULE] Subject–verb agreement with singular noun

[Q1332] Select the sentence that contains a grammatical error from the options below:
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A. The committee had already decided to postpone the meeting.
(b) B. The committee had already decided to postponed the meeting.
(c) C. The committee had already decided to postpone the meeting.
(d) D. The committee had already decided to postpone the meeting.
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule in English: The verb form after a modal or auxiliary should be the base form. "postponed" is a past participle; the correct base form is "postpone".
उदा. गलत: वह गया था; सही: वह गया है।
[RULE] Verb Form after Auxiliary

[Q1333] The committee members have presented their reports after the meeting. The number of participants who attended the seminar was impressive. Each of the students' opinions seems to be considered carefully. The list of items, including the pens and notebooks, are on the table.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] d
[SOL]
In (D), the subject is the singular noun ‘list’, hence the verb should be ‘is’ not ‘are’. The phrase ‘including the pens and notebooks’ is a non‑restrictive clause and does not affect agreement.
उदाहरण: The list of items, including the pens and notebooks, is on the table.
[RULE] Subject‑verb agreement with singular subject

[Q1334] Choose the sentence that contains an error in pronoun‑antecedent agreement: Every student should submit his assignment by Friday. Neither of the options has worked for her. The committee has decided to postpone its meeting. The couple, whose wedding photo was taken last year, is planning a trip.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In (A), ‘every student’ is singular but ‘his’ is masculine; the correct pronoun is ‘his or her’ or ‘their’. 
उदाहरण: Every student should submit their assignment by Friday.
[RULE] Pronoun–antecedent agreement (singular vs plural, gender)

[Q1335] Identify the sentence with a misplaced modifier: The teacher explained the concept to the students, which was appreciated. The students, who were tired, finished the exam quickly. The manager, after reviewing the report, has decided to hire more staff. The chef, cooking the meal, was unaware of the allergy.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] a
[SOL]
In (A), the clause ‘which was appreciated’ incorrectly attaches to ‘students’ instead of the action of explaining. It should read: The teacher explained the concept, which was appreciated by the students.
उदाहरण: The teacher explained the concept, which was appreciated by the students.
[RULE] Misplaced or dangling modifier

[Q1336] Which sentence contains an error in the use of a comparative adjective? John is taller than his brother. The new policy is more efficient than the old one. She is the bestest performer in the team. This solution is cheaper than the previous one.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] c
[SOL]
In (C), ‘bestest’ is not a correct comparative form. The correct comparative is ‘best’ (superlative) or ‘better’ (comparative). 
उदाहरण: She is the best performer in the team.
[RULE] Comparative and superlative forms

[Q1337] Choose the sentence that contains an error in comma usage: He bought apples, oranges, and bananas at the market. After the lecture, the students left the hall. The manager, who had been absent, was not present. The report, which was due yesterday, has been submitted.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D

[SOL]
In (C), the comma after ‘manager’ is unnecessary because the clause ‘who had been absent’ is essential for identifying which manager. It should read: The manager who had been absent was not present.
उदाहरण: The manager who had been absent was not present.
[RULE] Comma usage with restrictive vs non‑restrictive clauses

(a) Option A

[Q1339] Which sentence contains an error in verb tense consistency? She has been working on the project since yesterday. They will finish the report by tomorrow. The manager had given the instructions, and every one has started working. The team is planning to launch the product next month.

(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D

In (C), the past perfect ‘had given’ is followed by present perfect ‘has started’, breaking tense consistency. It should be ‘had started’.

[Q1423] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[RULE] Past perfect + would for future in past

[Q1427] Choose the correct sentence: "She has been working at the firm for( A) five years( B) since 2018( C) and has received( D) several promotions.

(d) Impeccable

[SOL]
The phrase ‘for five years since 2018’ is redundant; either ‘for five years’ or ‘since 2018’ should be used. The comma before ‘and’ is unnecessary. 
उदाहरण: She has been working at the firm for five years and has received several promotions.
[RULE] Redundancy in time expressions; comma usage

[Q1428] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[SOL]

The clause ‘which was delayed by two months and was eventually completed’ is a non‑restrictive relative clause and needs commas around it.

[RULE] Modal Verb Construction

[Q1506] Read the following passage and The cat is sleeping under the table. Please bring the documents to the office. We are going to the beach and we will have a picnic. The student’s performance was very good. Which segment contains an error?
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Segment (C) contains a comma splice: two independent clauses joined only by a comma. It should be separated by a semicolon or conjunction.

Rule: Independent clauses must not be joined by a comma alone.
उदाहरण: "We are going to the beach; we will have a picnic."
[RULE] Comma Splice

[Q1507] Read the following passage and There are many reasons for the delay. The team, as well as the coach, were disappointed. I have visited many countries. She has been working here for three years. Which segment contains an error?
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Segment (B) has a subject‑verb disagreement: the compound subject *team* and *coach* is singular, so the verb should be *was*.

Rule: Singular compound subject takes singular verb.
उदाहरण: "The team, as well as the coach, **was** disappointed."
[RULE] Subject‑Verb Agreement with Compound Subjects

[Q1508] Read the following passage and The in form at i on was shared with the public. He gave me a book, and I looked at it. We will attend the meeting tomorrow. They had been waiting for the announcement. Which segment contains an error?
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Segment (A) incorrectly places the article *the* before *information*, which is uncountable. It should be omitted.

Rule: Uncountable nouns do not require an article in the singular form.
उदाहरण: "The **information** was shared with the public."
[RULE] Use of Articles with Uncountable Nouns

[Q1509] Read the following passage and The manager asked me if I was ready. She has been working here since 2010. The students had completed the assignments and they were ready to submit. The weather had been very hot, therefore we went to the pool. Which segment contains an error?
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] d
[SOL]
Segment (D) uses *therefore* incorrectly; the correct conjunction is *so* or *therefore* should be followed by a comma.

Rule: Conjunctions like *therefore* need proper punctuation and placement.
उदाहरण: "The weather had been very hot, **so** we went to the pool."
[RULE] Conjunction Usage and Punctuation

[Q1510] Read the following passage and He is a good student, but he sometimes forgets his home work. The data shows a significant rise in temperature. The committee has been meeting every week. She was the best player of the team. Which segment contains an error?
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] d
[SOL]
Segment (D) uses *of* after *best* incorrectly. It should be *in*.

Rule: *Best* as a superlative is followed by *in*, not *of*.
उदाहरण: "She was the best player **in** the team."
[RULE] Superlative Preposition Usage

[Q1511] Read the following passage and The teacher asked the students to submit the assignments. She has been learning English since she was five years old. They have to finish the project by Friday. The city has increased its population by 10%. Which segment contains an error?
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Segment (B) incorrectly uses *since* with a period of time. It should be *for*.

Rule: *Since* is used for a starting point; *for* indicates duration.
उदाहरण: "She has been learning English **for** five years."
[RULE] Use of Since vs For

[Q1512] Read the following passage and The students had completed the test before the clock struck noon. He was walking home when he realised that he had lost his keys. The report was submitted to the manager. The results were the best in the sector. Which segment contains an error?
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XII (2024)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] d
[SOL]
Segment (D) uses *the* before *best* incorrectly. The superlative *best* does not require an article.

Rule: Superlatives do not take *the* when used alone.
उदाहरण: "The results were **best** in the sector."
[RULE] Superlative Article Usage

[Q1543] The team of researchers, who has been working on the project for months, finally presented their findings at the conference.

[Q1544] Neither the manager nor the employees were satisfied with the decision, but they was given a chance to appeal.

[Q1546] The committee has decided that the new policy shall be implemented immediately, and it will be enforced by the 30th of the month.
[EXAM: SSC Selection Post Phase XIV (2026)]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) The committee has decided that the new policy shall be implemented immediately, and it will be enforced by the 30th of the month.
(b) The committee has decided that the new policy shall be implemented immediately, and it will be enforced by 30th of the month.
(c) The committee has decided that the new policy shall be implemented immediately, and it will be enforced by the 30th month.
(d) The committee has decided that the new policy shall be implemented immediately, and it will be enforced by the 30th of month.
[ANS] a

Segment B incorrectly uses "that was collected". The relative pronoun should be "that was collected" is acceptable, but the error is the unnecessary past tense in the relative clause; it should be "that was collected" is fine. Actually the error is the missing comma after "data"? The correct sentence: "The data, which was collected during the experiment, was analyzed." The error is omission of comma.

उदाहरण: डेटा, जिसे प्रयोग के दौरान एकत्र किया गया, का विश्लेषण किया गया।
[RULE] Use of Commas with Non‑restrictive Clauses

[Q1605] Identify the sentence that contains a pronoun error.

(b) Tenacious
(c) Vibrant
(d) Lucid

[SOL]

[Q1614] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

(b) The team of engineers have completed the new bridge.
(c) The teams of engineers has completed the new bridge.
(d) The team of engineers completed the new bridge.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When the subject is a collective noun such as ‘team’, the verb takes singular form. Hence, ‘has’ is correct. In Hindi: ‘टीम’ एकवचन है, इसलिए क्रिया भी एकवचन होनी चाहिए।

[Q1615] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier-1]

(b) She don’t know the answer to the question.
(c) She doesn’t knows the answer to the question.
(d) She don’t knows the answer to the question.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The auxiliary verb ‘do’ in negative sentences is ‘doesn’t’ for third person singular. The verb after it remains in base form. Hindi: ‘doesn’t’ का प्रयोग ‘she’ के साथ किया जाता है।
[RULE] Negative contraction for third person singular

[Q1616] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Neither the manager nor the staff was informed about the delay.
(b) Neither the manager nor the staff were informed about the delay.
(c) Neither the manager nor the staff were informing about the delay.
(d) Neither the manager nor the staff was informing about the delay.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
When two subjects are joined by ‘neither…nor’, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, which is singular ‘staff’. Hence ‘was’ is correct. Hindi: ‘neither…nor’ के बाद का क्रिया निकटतम संज्ञा के साथ मेल खाना चाहिए।
[RULE] Verb agreement with ‘neither…nor’

[Q1617] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

(a) The committee has decided to hold the meeting next week, however, the members have not yet responded.
(b) The committee has decided to hold the meeting next week; however, the members have not yet responded.
(c) The committee has decided to hold the meeting next week, however the members have not yet responded.
(d) The committee has decided to hold the meeting next week; however the members have not yet responded.
[ANS] b
[SOL]
A semicolon is required before ‘however’ when it introduces an independent clause. In Hindi: ‘however’ से पहले अर्धविराम का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
[RULE] Use of semicolon before ‘however’

[Q1619] Spot the error in the following sentence: "John, along with his colleagues, has worked on the project for two years.

Wrong modal: ‘could not be’ should be ‘could not be held’. The phrase needs the auxiliary ‘be’ before ‘held’. 
उदाहरण: ‘...that the event **could not be held** on time.’
[RULE] Modal + passive construction

[Q1665] The in form at i on provided by the auditor was accurate.

(a) Segment (A)

(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)

[Q1666] Choose the segment which contains an error: The committee has decided to postpone the meeting. The committee has decided to postpone the meetings. The committees has decided to postpone the meeting. The committee decided to postpone the meeting.

(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D

[SOL]
Subject‑Verb Agreement.
The subject ‘The committees’ is plural, so the verb should be ‘have’ instead of ‘has’.
हिंदी उदाहरण: ‘समिति के सदस्यों ने’ के बाद ‘हैं’ का प्रयोग होता है।

[Q1667] She has gone to the market. She has gone to the markets. She has gone to the market. She has gone to the market yesterday.

(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D

[SOL]
Temporal adverb placement.
When an adverb of time is used, it should be placed after the main verb or at the end of the sentence. ‘Yesterday’ should come after the verb.
हिंदी उदाहरण: ‘मैं कल दुकान गया’ – ‘कल’ अंत में आता है।

(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Subject‑Verb Agreement.
‘Students’ is plural; the verb should be ‘are’ not ‘is’.
हिंदी उदाहरण: ‘छात्रा’ बहुवचन है तो ‘हैं’ प्रयोग होता है।
[RULE] Subject‑Verb Agreement

[Q1669] Choose the segment with the error: If I was you, I would take that job. If I were you, I would take that job. If I were you, I would take that job. If I was you, I would take that job.

(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Subjunctive Mood.
In ‘If I were you’ the correct form is ‘were’; ‘was’ is incorrect.
हिंदी उदाहरण: ‘अगर मैं तुम्हारी जगह होता’ – ‘हूं’ नहीं, ‘होता’।

[Q1670] Identify the erroneous segment: The book, which I bought yesterday, is excellent. The book, who I bought yesterday, is excellent. The book, which I bought yesterday, is excellent. The book, which I bought yesterday, is excellent.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Relative pronoun usage.
‘Book’ is an object, so ‘which’ is correct; ‘who’ is for people.
हिंदी उदाहरण: ‘किताब’ के लिए ‘जिसका’ प्रयोग होता है, ‘जो’ नहीं।

[Q1671] Choose the segment that contains an error: He enjoys cooking but does not enjoy baking. He enjoys cooking but does not enjoy baking. He enjoys cooking but does not enjoy baking. He enjoys cooking but does not enjoy baking.

(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] d
[SOL]
Parallel structure.
Both verbs after ‘enjoys’ should be in the same form: ‘enjoys’ not ‘does not enjoy’.
हिंदी उदाहरण: ‘उसे खाना बनाना अच्छा लगता है’ – दोनों क्रिया एक समान होनी चाहिए।

[Q1672] The company has been established in 1998. The company has been established in 1998. The company has been established in 1998. The company has been established in 1998.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Tense consistency.
‘Established’ is past participle, but the time expression ‘in 1998’ should use simple past: ‘was established’.
हिंदी उदाहरण: ‘1998 में स्थापित हुई’ – ‘was established’।

[Q1673] Choose the segment containing the error: The outcome was better than expected. The outcome was better than expected. The outcome was better than expected. The outcome was better than expected.

(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Comparative structure.
‘Better than expected’ requires ‘better than’ to be followed by a noun or pronoun; ‘than expected’ is acceptable but ‘better than expected’ is correct – no error actually.
हिंदी उदाहरण: ‘उम्मीद से बेहतर’ – सही है।
[RULE] Comparative Construction

[Q1674] Identify the erroneous segment: She likes reading, and she also likes writing. She likes reading, and she also likes writing. She likes reading, and she also likes writing. She likes reading, and she also likes writing.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D

[SOL]
Ambiguous use of ‘also’.
‘Also’ is redundant after ‘and’; better to use ‘too’ or remove one conjunction.
हिंदी उदाहरण: ‘वह पढ़ना पसंद करती है और लिखना भी पसंद करती है’ – ‘भी’ से ‘और’ हटाया जा सकता है।
[RULE] Conjunction Usage

[Q1675] He had finished his home work before dinner. He had finished his home work before dinner. He had finished his home work before dinner. He had finished his home work before dinner.

(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] d
[SOL]
Sequence of tenses.
The past perfect ‘had finished’ is appropriate only when the action occurred before another past action; here ‘before dinner’ is fine but the usage is correct. Actually no error.
हिंदी उदाहरण: ‘उसने खाना खाने से पहले होमवर्क पूरा कर लिया।’ – सही है।
[RULE] Past Perfect Tense

[Q1676] Choose the segment with the error: The project was completed by the team. The project was completed by the team. The project was completed by the team. The project was completed by the team.

[Q1677] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1688] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1689] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) The word "suggested" should be "suggested that".
(b) The verb "goes" should be "go".
(c) "the museum" should be "a museum".
(d) "Saturday" should be "sunday".
[ANS] b
[SOL]
After a verb of suggestion followed by that-clause, the verb in the clause is in the base form, not the third person singular.

[RULE] Verb form after verbs of suggestion + that-clause

[Q1690] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier-1]

(d) "Received" should be "receives".
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The pronoun must refer to the singular noun "committee"; therefore, the correct pronoun is "it".
उदाहरण: "... but **it** has not received the reply..."
[RULE] Pronoun agreement with collective nouns

[Q1691] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) "Three months" should be "three month".
(b) "Will finish" should be "would finish".
(c) "Next week" should be "next week" (no change).
(d) "Has been working" should be "had been working".
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The past perfect continuous is needed because the action started before another past event (the week). So it should be "had been working".
उदाहरण: "...for three months and **had been working** on it..."
[RULE] Use of past perfect continuous

[Q1692] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier-1]

(d) "Too low" should be "too high".

In a second conditional, the main clause uses the modal verb "would"; the infinitive following "would" should be base form. The sentence is correct as written, so there is no error. However, the question assumes an error; the best choice is option 1, which is actually correct. Hence, option 1 is the answer to identify the error (none).
💡 हिन्दी व्याख्या: सही विकल्प '"Would not take" should be "will not take".' है। वाक्य के व्याकरणिक नियमों के अनुसार इसे शुद्ध किया गया है।

[Q1693] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1694] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1695] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1696] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1697] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1698] The team of experts, who are well known, for their innovative research, has presented a comprehensive report. The present at i on was well received.

(d) Segment (D)

[Q1699] She will be arriving at 10 p.m., after she finished her home work, and will then start her assignment. The schedule is set for the evening.

(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)

[Q1700] Spot the grammatical mistake: The committee has decided to postpone the meeting, because the chairman’s presence is required. They will reschedule it next week. The decision is final.

(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)

[SOL]

[Q1701] Which segment has an error? All of the students, who are from different states, have brought their own lunch. They will be sharing the snacks. The event is scheduled for tomorrow.

(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: The relative clause is non-restrictive and should be set off by commas. The comma after 'students' is correct, but the clause itself is fine. However, the main error is that 'students' is plural and the verb should be 'have' (already correct). The real error is missing article before 'different states'.
उदा. हिंदी: "from different states" में 'the' नहीं होना चाहिए, अतः "from different states" सही है।

[Q1702] The manager, who has been working here for five years, will be leaving tomorrow. He has been instrumental in many projects. His departure will be a loss for the company.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: The relative clause 'who has been working' is correct. However, the main clause incorrectly uses 'will be leaving' for a future action; it should use simple present 'leaves' for scheduled events.
उदा. हिंदी: "He leaves tomorrow" सही है, "He will be leaving tomorrow" गलत है।
[RULE] Future Simple vs. Present Simple for Scheduled Events

---

[Q1703] Spot the error in the following: Each of the participants was given a clipboard. The supervisor will distribute the forms. They will fill them out in the session. The forms are ready for submission.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule in English: 'Each' is singular, so the verb should be singular. Segment (B) uses 'will distribute' in future tense which is acceptable, but the error is elsewhere: Segment (C) uses 'they will fill' which conflicts with singular subject in (A). The correct verb form should be 'fills' in (C).
उदा. हिंदी: "Each participant fills" सही है, "Each participant fill" गलत है।
[RULE] Singular vs. Plural Verb Agreement

---

[Q1704] Which segment contains a mistake? The committee had reached a consensus. On the basis of the data, they will revise the policy. The revision will be implemented next month. The stakeholders will be notified.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule in English: The adverbial phrase 'On the basis of the data' should be placed before the main clause or within commas. The comma after 'data' creates a comma splice. It should be a semi-colon or a period.
उदा. हिंदी: "On the basis of the data; they will revise" सही है, "On the basis of the data, they will revise" गलत है।
[RULE] Comma Splice / Adverbial Placement

[Q1705] Find the erroneous segment: The report, which was due last week, has been submitted by the analyst. The findings are attached below. The analysis will be reviewed tomorrow.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: A non-restrictive relative clause uses commas. However, the clause 'which was due last week' is correct. The real error is missing article before 'report' – it should be 'The report' (already present). The mistake is that the verb tense in (B) should be simple past 'was submitted', not present perfect 'has been submitted', because the action happened last week.
उदा. हिंदी: "was submitted" सही है, "has been submitted" अनावश्यक है।
[RULE] Tense Consistency

[Q1706] Which part of the sentence is wrong? The project will start next Monday. The team, who are prepared for the challenge, will tackle the objectives. The schedule is confirmed.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule in English: The relative clause 'who are prepared' is fine, but the comma after 'team' incorrectly sets off the clause. It should be a restrictive clause without commas because it identifies the specific team.
उदा. हिंदी: "The team who are prepared" सही है, "The team, who are prepared" गलत है।
[RULE] Restrictive vs. Non-Restrictive Clauses

[Q1707] Spot the error: The manager will be presenting the new policy. The policy will be adopted after the meeting. The documentation is ready. The staff will receive a copy today.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: The verb phrase 'will be presenting' is future continuous, which is acceptable. However, the error lies in the missing article before 'new policy' – it should be 'the new policy'.
उदा. हिंदी: "the new policy" सही है, "new policy" गलत है।
[RULE] Article Usage

[Q1708] The data, which has been collected, will be analyzed by the research team. The results will be published soon. The findings will be available online.
[EXAM: SSC CPO 2025]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: The non-restrictive relative clause 'which has been collected' is correct. However, the main error is that the verb tense in (B) should be simple future 'will analyze', not present perfect 'has been analyzed', because the analysis is yet to occur.
उदा. हिंदी: "will analyze" सही है, "has been analyzed" गलत है।
[RULE] Tense Consistency

(b) Option B

(a) Option A

[Q1719] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1720] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1721] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1723] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[SOL]
When a verb follows *neither…nor*, it agrees with the noun closest to it. Here *employees* is plural, so the verb should be plural *are*.

[Q1724] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1725] The committee has decided to postpone the meeting, however, it will be rescheduled next week.

(d) Munificent
[ANS] a
[SOL]
A comma is required before a compound‑sentence conjunction *however* when it introduces a new independent clause.
उदाहरण: She is tired, however she will still attend.

When describing a relative clause that refers to *who*, the verb should be past tense to match the main clause. *Had* is correct.

[Q1730] Spot the error in the following passage: The team of scientists had decided to publish their results in the international journal. The first paper was rejected because of lack of data, but they kept trying. They eventually succeeded, and the paper was well received by the community. (a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The error is in sentence (A). It should be "The team of scientists had decided to publish their results in an international journal." The article "a" is required before a non-specific noun.

नियम: न-विशिष्ट संज्ञा से पहले अनिश्चित लेख "a" या "an" का प्रयोग किया जाता है। उदाहरण: "an international journal".
[RULE] Use of indefinite article

[Q1731] Spot the error in the following passage: The newly elected governor visited the old factory. He inspected the machinery and noticed that the workers were not following the safety protocols. The governor ordered immediate closure of the plant. The closure was delayed because the workers had taken a strike. Which of the following sentences contains an error?

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Option A
(b) Option B
(c) Option C
(d) Option D
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The error is in sentence (B). The correct form is "not following" is fine, but the sentence is awkward. The intended meaning is that the workers were not following protocols, which is correct. However, the error lies in sentence (D): "The closure was delayed because the workers had taken a strike." The past perfect "had taken" is unnecessary; simple past "took" is correct.

नियम: Simple past tense is used for completed actions in the past. उदाहरण: "The workers took a strike."
[RULE] Past tense usage

[Q1740] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

[Q1741] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

The pronoun "which" refers to the data (plural) but is used as singular. The correct pronoun is "that" or "who" is not applicable. Use "that".
उदा. "The data are consistent with the hypothesis that suggests a strong correlation."
[RULE] Pronoun Reference

[Q1782] Read the paragraph below and choose the segment that contains an error. I have seen him yesterday at the market. I have seen him yesterday at the market. I have seen him yesterday at the market. I have seen him yesterday at the market.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2024]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) (A)
(b) (B)
(c) (C)
(d) (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The verb tense is wrong. "I saw him yesterday" uses simple past. "Have seen" is present perfect, which should not be combined with a specific time. Correct sentence: "I saw him yesterday at the market."
उदा. "I saw him yesterday at the market."
[RULE] Tense Agreement

[Q1783] Read the paragraph below and choose the segment that contains an error. The books on the shelf are arranged by author, which is unusual. The books on the shelf are arranged by author, which is unusual. The books on the shelf are arranged by author, which is unusual. The books on the shelf are arranged by author, which is unusual.
[EXAM: SSC MTS 2024]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) (A)
(b) (B)
(c) (C)
(d) (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The relative pronoun "which" is used incorrectly. It should be "that" or better: "The books on the shelf are arranged by author; this is unusual."
उदा. "The books on the shelf are arranged by author; this is unusual."
[RULE] Relative Pronoun

[Q1784] Read the paragraph below and choose the segment that contains an error. The committee will decide the new policy next week, and the members will vote. The committee will decide the new policy next week, and the members will vote. The committee will decide the new policy next week, and the members will vote. The committee will decide the new policy next week, and the members will vote.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) (A)
(b) (B)
(c) (C)
(d) (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
This is a comma splice. Two independent clauses are joined by a comma. Replace the comma with a semicolon or add a conjunction.
उदा. "The committee will decide the new policy next week; the members will vote."
[RULE] Comma Splice

[Q1785] Read the paragraph below and choose the segment that contains an error. The project, which has been delayed, will be completed by next month. (a) (A)
(b) (B)
(c) (C)
(d) (D)

उदा. "The project, delayed, will be completed by next month."

[Q1786] The committee has decided to postpone the meeting. She will be arriving at 10 a.m. tomorrow. The students were given a chance to present their projects. The books was placed on the shelf.

(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D

[SOL]
The error is in segment (D) – the subject ‘books’ is plural, so the verb should be ‘were’ not ‘was’. Correct sentence: "The books were placed on the shelf."

Rule: Subject–verb agreement – the verb must agree in number with the subject.
उदाहरण: "पुस्तकें शेल्फ पर रखी गईं।"

[Q1787] He has been working on the report since morning. They had finished the assignment before the dead line The manager will speak at the conference to night I seen the movie last week.

(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D
[ANS] d
[SOL]
Segment (D) contains the error – the past tense of ‘see’ is ‘saw’, not ‘seen’. Correct: "I saw the movie last week."

Rule: Simple past tense – use the irregular past form.

[Q1788] The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. She is going to the market to buy some vegetables. The project was completed on time by the team. He like to read books after dinner.

(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D

[SOL]
Segment (D) is wrong – after the verb ‘like’ the subject ‘he’ requires the base form ‘likes’. Correct: "He likes to read books after dinner."

Rule: Third person singular – add ‘s’ or ‘es’ to the base verb.
उदाहरण: "वह किताबें पढ़ना पसंद करता है।"

[Q1789] The new policy will be implemented next month. The results of the experiment were inconclusive. We has decided to postpone the trip. She has finished all her assignments.

(c) C
(d) D

[Q1790] The children were playing in the park. He has been working on his thesis all week. The government will announce the new policy tomorrow. It were raining when we left the house.

(b) B
(c) C
(d) D

Rule: Subject–verb agreement with impersonal subjects.
उदाहरण: "जब हम घर से निकले तो बरस रहा था।"
[RULE] Subject–verb agreement

[Q1791] The teacher asked the students to submit their assignments. She is going to attend the meeting at 3 p.m. The dogs barked loudly at the mailman. The cake will baked tomorrow by the chef.

(d) D

[Q1792] The report was submitted on time. They have been working on the project for months. The manager will review the proposals tomorrow. She are going to the cinema to night

(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D

Rule: Verb agreement with singular third person.

[Q1793] The team has finished their project. He will be arriving at the station at 6 p.m. She has been studying French for years. The children was excited about the trip.

(b) B
(c) C
(d) D

[Q1794] She will finish the assignment by tomorrow. They have been reviewing the documents for hours. The project will be completed next week. I have went to the market earlier.

[Q1795] The new policy will be implemented next month. She had finished the book before the dead line The students were given a chance to present their projects. He likes to play cricket in the evening.

(a) A

(c) C
(d) D

[Q1796] The following sentences contain a grammatical error. She has been studying for three hours. He goes to the market every Sunday. They will finish the project by next week. We have visited Paris last year.

(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] d
[SOL]
Rule: When referring to a completed action in the past, use simple past tense, not present perfect.

उदाहरण: We visited Paris last year (सही) बजाय We have visited Paris last year (गलत).
[RULE] Tense consistency – present perfect vs simple past

[Q1797] The committee will discuss the proposal tomorrow. She had been waiting for an hour when the bus finally came. If I will have time, I will call you. He has finished his home work.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Rule: In conditional sentences with a future scenario, use ‘will’ in the main clause but not in the if‑clause.

उदाहरण: If I have time, I will call you (सही) बजाय If I will have time, I will call you (गलत).
[RULE] Conditional sentence structure

[Q1798] The children have played in the garden. I have known her for five years. She is reading a book that was written by her favorite author. They had walked for hours before they reached the station.

[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule: In the present perfect continuous, the verb should be ‘have been’ with a continuous form. The correct form is ‘have been playing’.

उदाहरण: They have been playing in the garden (सही) बजाय They have played in the garden (गलत).
[RULE] Present perfect continuous tense

---

[Q1799] Which segment contains the error? He had left the house early in the morning. She have never seen such a beautiful sight. The results of the test are out. I had finished my work when the alarm rang.

(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule: In the simple past tense, the verb should be in past form. ‘Have’ should be ‘had’.

उदाहरण: She had never seen such a beautiful sight (सही) बजाय She have never seen such a beautiful sight (गलत).
[RULE] Simple past tense agreement

[Q1800] The teacher explained the lesson clearly. It was raining when we left the house. The news that the company had been acquired was shocking. He will having finished his assignment, he left early.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] d
[SOL]
Rule: After ‘will’, the base form of the verb should be used. ‘Will have finished’ is correct.

उदाहरण: He will have finished his assignment, he left early (सही) बजाय He will having finished his assignment, he left early (गलत).
[RULE] Future perfect tense

[Q1801] She has seen the movie, and it was amazing. We had been going to the park when it started to rain. He will finish the project if he is given more resources. The students had studied for the test, but they didn’t perform well.

(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule: In a past perfect continuous, the verb should be ‘had been’ + present participle. The correct form is ‘had been going’.

उदाहरण: They had been going to the park (सही) बजाय They had been going to the park (सही). (Note: this example shows correct usage; the erroneous sentence used ‘been going’ incorrectly.)
[RULE] Past perfect continuous tense

[Q1802] Which segment contains the error? I have never seen such a strange phenomenon. If she will finish early, she will join us. He had been working for ten hours before he took a break. The team has been winning the championship for the last five seasons.

(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)
[ANS] b
[SOL]
Rule: In conditional sentences, use ‘will’ in the main clause only; the ‘if’ clause should use simple present.

उदाहरण: If she finishes early, she will join us (सही) बजाय If she will finish early, she will join us (गलत).

[Q1803] The book has been read by many students. They have lived in this city for five years. The manager will having finished the report, he left. She has been working here since 2010.

(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)

[SOL]
Rule: After ‘will’, use the base form of the verb. The correct form is ‘will have finished’.

उदाहरण: She will have finished the report, she left (सही) बजाय She will having finished the report, she left (गलत).
[RULE] Future perfect tense

[Q1804] Which segment contains the error? The children was playing in the courtyard. The train is arriving at 6 pm. We have visited the museum last year. She will be studying at 7 pm tomorrow.

(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)

[SOL]
Rule: The verb must agree with the plural subject. Use ‘were’ with plural subjects.

[Q1805] He had been working on the project for two months. The dog that had barked all night was finally quiet. She will having arrived, she called for help. We had finished the assignment before the dead line
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)

[SOL]
Rule: After ‘will’, use the base form of the verb. The correct form is ‘will have arrived’.

[Q1806] The committee has decided to reorganise the entire system by the end of this year. This decision will benefit every one.

(a) Option A
(b) Option B

[SOL]
Subject-Verb Agreement: *has decided* is singular, but *committee* is a collective noun that takes singular verb.
उदाहरण: The committee *has* decided (सही) / The committee *have* decided (गलत).

[Q1807] Choose the segment with the error: The children were excited about the upcoming field trip to the Science Museum. They will start the trip at 9 AM.

(a) Option A

[SOL]
Capitalisation Rule: *the* should be capitalised after a preposition.
उदाहरण: The children were excited about *the* upcoming field trip (सही) / The children were excited about *The* upcoming field trip (गलत).

[Q1808] Find the erroneous part: She has been working on the project for two months and she has finished it.

[Q1810] Identify the error: They plans to launch the new product next month. Every one is eager to see it.

[Q1811] Choose the part containing an error: The meeting will begin at 10 o’clock and will last for two hours.

(a) Option A

[Q1814] Our team has completed the tasks and it is proud of the results.

[Q1815] Choose the incorrect part: The manager, who was appointed last year, will visit the site tomorrow.

[Q1818] Segment : He **are** the best player of the team. Identify the error.

[Q1819] Segment : There was **many** reasons for the delay. Identify the error.

[Q1820] Segment : The committee **have** decided to postpone the event. Identify the error.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) has
(b) have decided
(c) committee
(d) postpone

Subject–verb agreement: ‘committee’ is singular, so the verb should be *has*.

[Q1821] Segment : I have **seen** him yesterday. Identify the error.

(a) have
(b) seen
(c) him

[Q1822] Segment : Every one should bring **their** own lunch. Identify the error.

(a) their

[Q1823] Segment : The news **was** that the company will be launching a new product next month. Identify the error.

(a) was that
(b) was
(c) news
(d) company
[ANS] a
[SOL]

(d) available

[Q1837] Spot the error in the following sentence: "She has went to the market yesterday.

(b) She has went to the market yesterday.
(c) Dubious
(d) Ephemeral
[ANS] a
[SOL]

[Q1838] Identify the grammatical mistake in: "The group of students was waiting for the bus.

(b) The group of students was waiting for the bus.
(c) Kinetic
(d) Lethargic

[SOL]

[ANS] b
[SOL]

[Q1841] Spot the error in: "Neither of the boys are ready to leave.

[Q1843] Spot the error in: "She is the most intelligent of the class.

[Q1846] He have been working on the project for two weeks.

[Q1847] The committee was discussed the proposal yesterday.

[Q1848] She is more taller than her brother.

(d) D. The sentence needs a comma after 'She'.
[ANS] a
[SOL]

[Q1849] I will go to the market, and buy some fruits.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier-2]

(b) B. The conjunction 'and' is unnecessary.
(c) C. The comma splice is acceptable.
(d) D. The sentence should be split into two sentences.
[ANS] a
[SOL]
Rule in English: A comma cannot join two independent clauses; use a semicolon or a conjunction without a comma.
उदा. Hindi explanation: दो स्वतंत्र वाक्यांशों को कॉमा से जोड़ना गलत है; इसलिए सेमी‑कोलन या बिना कॉमा के संयोजन प्रयोग करें।
[RULE] Comma Splice

[Q1850] Neither the students nor the teacher were aware of the change.
[EXAM: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier-2]

(c) C. The conjunction 'nor' is wrong; it should be 'and'.
(d) D. The sentence requires a comma after 'teacher'.

[Q1853] There is many reasons to visit the museum.

[Q1854] I would rather go for a walk, than stay inside.

[Q1856] The team of scientists, who has been working on the project for two years, presented their findings. (a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)

[SOL]
The relative pronoun ‘who’ refers to ‘team’ which is a collective noun but considered singular. Hence, the verb should be ‘has been’ in the clause. However, the main clause ‘presented’ is correct. The correct segment is (C) where ‘have been’ is used, matching the plural sense.
उदाहरण: ‘team’ को एकवचन माना जाता है, अतः ‘has been’ सही है।

[Q1857] She was excited about the results, which will be announced tomorrow. She was excited about the results, which were announced tomorrow. She was excited about the results, which will be announced tomorrow. She was excited about the results, which was announced tomorrow.

(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)

[SOL]
The relative pronoun ‘which’ refers to ‘results’ (plural), so the verb should be plural: ‘were announced’. Segment (D) incorrectly uses ‘was’. 
उदाहरण: ‘results’ बहुवचन है, अतः ‘were announced’ सही है।

[Q1858] Choose the segment that contains a grammatical error: The committee had decided to postpone the meeting. The committee had decided to postpone the meeting. (a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)
(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)

[SOL]
Segment (D) uses a comma before the conjunction ‘but’ linking two independent clauses, which requires a semicolon or a comma with a coordinating conjunction. The error is the comma splice.

(a) Segment (A)
(b) Segment (B)

(d) Segment (D)

[RULE] Use of commas with restrictive/non‑restrictive clauses

(c) Segment (C)
(d) Segment (D)

[Q1928] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:

(b) Replace 'all members were absent' with 'all members were present'
(c) Replace 'had' with 'has'
(d) Replace 'the new policy' with 'the new policies'

[SOL]

[SOL]

उदा. हिंदी में: "छात्र, जो थके हुए थे, जल्दी पहुंचे, लेकिन उन्हें आराम करने की अनुमति नहीं थी।"
[RULE] Subject-Verb Agreement (Plural Pronoun)

[Q1975] In the sentence "The data shows clear trends, however the analysis is flawed," the error is in segment .

[Q1978] In the sentence "The manager, who has been with the company for 10 years, has been well respected by his colleagues, and he was are known for his integrity," the error is in segment .

[Q1979] In the sentence "The students were excited about the trip, and they has packed their bags," the error is in segment .

(d) D. No error

[Q1980] A. The committee had conducted the survey last month and found that the majority of respondents were satisfied. B. The committee had conducted the survey last month and found that majority of respondents were satisfied. C. The committee had conducted the survey last month and found that the majority of respondents were satisfied. D. The committee had conducted the survey last month and found that the majority of respondents was satisfied.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D
[ANS] d
[SOL]
The subject ‘respondents’ is plural, therefore the verb must be plural as well.

उदाहरण: 
- गलत: The committee had conducted the survey last month and found that the majority of respondents was satisfied.
- सही: ... respondents were satisfied.
[RULE] Subject‑verb agreement (plural subject with plural verb)

[Q1981] A. She has been studying English for five years. B. She has been studying English for five years. C. She has been studying English for five years. D. She has been studying English for five years.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D
[ANS] a
[SOL]
All options are identical; the error is that the segment should be different. However, as per exam pattern, the intended error is the repetition of the same sentence. The correct answer points out that there is no variation, which is a mistake in the question itself.

उदाहरण: 
- सही: She has been studying English for five years.
- गलत: (No variation – error in question).
[RULE] Question design error (identical options)

[Q1982] A. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. B. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. C. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. D. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D
[ANS] b
[SOL]
The sentence is a pangram; the word ‘jumps’ should be ‘jumped’ to maintain past tense consistency with ‘foxes’ (plural).

उदाहरण: 
- गलत: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
- सही: The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog.
[RULE] Tense consistency (past tense)

[Q1983] A. Neither the manager nor the employees were satisfied with the decision. B. Neither the manager nor the employees was satisfied with the decision. C. Neither the manager nor the employees were satisfied with the decision. D. Neither the manager nor the employees is satisfied with the decision.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D
[ANS] b
[SOL]
With ‘neither‑nor’ construction, the verb agrees with the noun closest to it. Here, ‘employees’ is plural, so ‘were’ is correct.

उदाहरण: 
- गलत: Neither the manager nor the employees was satisfied.
- सही: Neither the manager nor the employees were satisfied.
[RULE] Verb agreement with neither…nor (closest noun)

[Q1984] A. The in form at i on has been gathered by the researchers. B. The in form at i on has been gathered by the researchers. C. The in form at i on has been gathered by the researchers. D. The in form at i on has been gathered by the researchers.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D
[ANS] c
[SOL]
The segment should use ‘has been’ because ‘information’ is a singular uncountable noun. Option C mistakenly uses ‘have been’ (plural).

उदाहरण: 
- गलत: The information have been gathered.
- सही: The information has been gathered.
[RULE] Singular vs plural verb with uncountable nouns
