[Q1985] Identify which segment contains an error: A. He has been working on the project for three months. B. He has been working on the project for three months. C. He has been working on the project for three months. D. He has been working on the project for three months.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The error lies in the use of the present perfect continuous tense with a fixed duration. The correct form is ‘has been working’ for a duration of three months.

उदाहरण: 
- गलत: He has been working for three months.
- सही: He has been working on the project for three months.
[RULE] Correct use of present perfect continuous with duration

[Q1986] A. The students who was late apologize to the teacher. B. The students who was late apologize to the teacher. C. The students who were late apologize to the teacher. D. The students who were late apologize to the teacher.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The relative clause ‘who was late’ uses a singular verb ‘was’ with the plural subject ‘students’. It should be ‘who were late’.

उदाहरण: 
- गलत: The students who was late.
- सही: The students who were late.
[RULE] Subject‑verb agreement in relative clauses

[Q1987] A. She has much books to read before the exam. B. She has many books to read before the exam. C. She has many books to read before the exam. D. She has many books to read before the exam.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D

[SOL]
‘Much’ is used with uncountable nouns; with countable ‘books’ we use ‘many’.

उदाहरण: 
- गलत: She has much books.
- सही: She has many books.
[RULE] Use of much vs many with countable/uncountable nouns

[Q1988] A. The data was collected from various sources. B. The data were collected from various sources. C. The data was collected from various sources. D. The data were collected from various sources.

(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D

‘Data’ is a plural noun in contemporary usage; the verb should be plural ‘were’.

[Q1989] A. If I had known, I would have acted differently. B. If I had known, I would have acted differently. C. If I had known, I would have acted differently. D. If I had known, I would have acted differently.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) A
(b) B
(c) C
(d) D
[ANS] d

The third conditional requires ‘had known’ and ‘would have acted’. The mistake is the omission of ‘had’ after ‘if’ in the conditional clause.

- सही: If I had known, I would have acted.
[RULE] Third conditional structure (if + past perfect, would have + past participle)

[Q1990] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-1]

(a) The research team has been working on the project for months and expects to finish it soon.

The subject "The research team" is singular, so the verb must be singular. The correct form is "expects".

(a) She gave the book and the paper to him, and the girl was very happy.

(c) She gave the book and the paper to him, and the girl were very happy.

(a) Both the students and the teacher was present at the meeting.
(b) Both the students and the teacher were present at the meeting.
(c) Both the students and the teacher is present at the meeting.

[Q1994] I went to the market, but I didn't bought any fruits.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]

(d) Obsolete

After "didn't" the base form of the verb is used, not the past tense. Correct: "buy".

[Q1995] Select the sentence that is grammatically correct from the options below:
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) The committee, along with the president, have decided to postpone the meeting.
(b) The committee, along with the president, has decided to postpone the meeting.
(c) The committee, along with the president, had decided to postpone the meeting.
(d) The committee, along with the president, will decide to postpone the meeting.

The main subject "The committee" is singular; the phrase "along with the president" is a prepositional phrase and does not change the subject. Correct: "has".

[Q1997] The students were asked to submit their assignments, and their teachers were also given a dead line

(a) The students were asked to submit their assignments, and *the* teachers were also given a deadline.

(c) The students were asked to submit their assignments, and their teachers were also given deadlines.
(d) Dubious
[ANS] c
[SOL]
Both nouns are plural, so the plural noun "deadlines" is appropriate. Correct: "deadlines".

[Q1998] He has a good knowledge of mathematics and physics.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-1]

(a) Kinetic
(b) He has a good knowledge of mathematics and physics.
(c) Lethargic
(d) Munificent

[SOL]
The noun "knowledge" is uncountable, so the article "a" should be omitted. Correct: "He has good knowledge of mathematics and physics."

[Q1999] Every one in the class has to submit their home work by Monday.
[EXAM: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-1]
[DIFFICULTY: Medium]
(a) Everyone in the class has to submit their homework by Monday.
(b) Everyone in the class has to submit *his or her* homework by Monday.
(c) Everyone in the class has to submit *their* homework by Monday.
(d) Redundant
[ANS] a
[SOL]
The singular pronoun "everyone" requires a singular possessive pronoun. The correct form is "his or her".
